metaDescription: The best dehumidifier under $100 for bedrooms, bathrooms and closets, compared on timers, defrost, tank size and how much moisture a small unit really removes.
expertTake: The Newo 44 oz is the best all-round pick, because its 24 to 96 hour timers and auto defrost make it forgiving for a room you do not visit daily. The BeOkay 58 oz is the value pick when you want the biggest tank. Anyone fighting a damp basement should not buy from this price band at all. If you are unsure, start with the Newo and keep the receipt, because a plate unit is the cheapest way to learn whether your room needs more machine than this price band can supply.
introParagraphs: Under the hundred dollar line you are buying a small appliance with a narrow job. It can take the edge off a stuffy bedroom, keep a bathroom from sweating or protect a closet, and it does that quietly and cheaply.

What it cannot do is dry a house. Knowing that before you buy saves a return and a season of disappointment. The $100 cap reflects listing prices on the date this guide was updated, and those prices move, so confirm before ordering.

products.name: Newo 44 oz small dehumidifier, 260 sq ft, 5 timers
products.description:
The Newo is a thermoelectric dehumidifier, which means a small cooled plate pulls moisture out of passing air and drips it into the tank. There is no compressor and no refrigerant, so it runs close to silent and weighs very little. What makes it the best overall pick is how many ways it lets you control run time: timers at 24, 48, 72 and 96 hours, or continuous operation, plus three working modes.

That range matters because most people do not need a machine running forever. A bathroom unit can be set for 24 hours after laundry, while a cabin unit can be set for 96 hours before you leave. Auto defrost protects the plate when the room gets cool, and a flashing red alert tells you when the tank is full. Against the 58 oz BeOkay you give up some tank, but you gain longer timers and a simpler alert system.

Expect a few seasons of use. Wipe the tank each time you empty it, rinse it with mild vinegar now and then, and keep dust off the intake. The ambient lights can be turned off. Do not ask it to dry a damp wall, because the plate moves ounces and the rating of 260 square feet is a ceiling for a closed, mildly damp room.
products.bestFor: Bathrooms, cabins and rooms used on and off.
pros: Timers from 24 to 96 hours or continuous
Auto defrost helps in cooler rooms
Flashing red light signals a full tank
cons: 44 oz tank fills in a humid week
Output is small compared with a compressor
260 sq ft rating is a ceiling

products.name: BeOkay 58 oz small dehumidifier, 230 sq ft, defrost
products.description:
The BeOkay carries the largest tank of the plate units at 58 oz, about 1657 ml. It uses the same thermoelectric approach as the Newo, with a defrost routine to keep the plate from icing and an auto shutoff when the tank is full. Three working modes and five timer settings give it enough control for a nursery or a small bedroom.

Its 230 square foot rating is the most modest in this guide, and that is a point in its favour: the claim matches what a small plate can do. If you want a unit that runs through a night and half a day without filling, the extra tank is the reason to choose it. Compared with the Newo, it gives you more capacity but fewer timer steps.

Care is simple. Rinse the tank, clear the vent and store it dry. In a room below about 60 degrees the plate slows noticeably, so keep it out of a cold garage. Treat it as a seasonal consumable and replace it when the output fades. A realistic expectation for the BeOkay is a nursery that feels less clammy overnight, not a room that changes character.
products.bestFor: Nurseries and small bedrooms that need a long run time.
pros: 58 oz tank is the largest of the group
cons: Fewer timer steps than the Newo

products.name: Windangel 44 oz small dehumidifier, 3 modes, auto defrost
products.description:
Windangel sells a 44 oz thermoelectric unit with three dehumidification modes, auto shutoff and auto defrost. It is the closest rival to the Newo, with the same tank size and the same safety features, but with a simpler control set. For people who dislike menus, that is a plus.

The sleep mode lowers fan speed for night use, and the normal mode runs at full pace. The ten colour lights are decoration and can be switched off. Compared with the BeOkay it has a smaller tank, so it fills sooner on a humid day.

Like every plate unit it is a consumable. Wipe the tank, keep the intake clear and replace it when output fades. It fits a closet, a bathroom or a small bedroom where humidity is moderate. If you are choosing between this and the Newo, ask yourself whether you will ever use a long timer. Many owners never do, and for them the cheaper, simpler unit is the better buy.
products.bestFor: Light use in small rooms where simple controls matter.
cons: 44 oz tank fills sooner than the BeOkay's

products.name: OWAAE dehumidifier, 1000 sq ft, sleep mode under 30 dB
products.description:
The OWAAE leads with sleep-mode noise, claiming under 30 dB, which is in the range of a quiet whisper. A plate and small fan can plausibly reach that level, since there is no compressor to hum. For a light sleeper that matters more than any other spec on the sheet.

The listing mentions enclosed spaces where humidity builds, which is the right use. The 1000 square foot rating should be read as a ceiling for a closed room, not a promise for a basement. Against the Newo it gives up the long timers but gains a quieter profile.

Treat the noise figure as a seller claim and judge it in your own room. Empty the tank, wipe it and dust the vents on schedule. Place it on a hard shelf away from the bed frame, because the buzz of a thin shelf is more audible than the fan itself. A cloth or foam pad under the base cuts vibration noise. Keep a hygrometer in the room so you know the claim holds, and return it if the room never improves.
cons: Noise figure is a seller claim
Same plate limits as the others

products.name: TABYIK 35 oz dehumidifier, 280 sq ft, auto shutoff
products.description:
The TABYIK is the plainest unit here: a 35 oz clear tank, a 280 square foot rating and auto shutoff. It exists for a first try in a closet or small bathroom. If it helps, you have learned that a larger unit will help more.

Compared with the Newo, it has a smaller tank and no timers. Its separate light button lets you switch the glow off.

Wipe the tank, rinse with vinegar occasionally and expect a short service life. At this level, that is acceptable. Because it is so inexpensive, it is worth buying one as a diagnostic: run it in the suspect closet for two weeks and watch the tank. If it fills every day, the space has a moisture source that needs fixing. If it barely collects water, the problem was minor and you can stop worrying.
products.bestFor: A first try in a closet or small bathroom.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The Newo offers 24, 48, 72 and 96 hour timers, which saves power and prevents a unit running dry in an empty room. Without a timer you rely on auto shutoff when the tank fills. If you travel, pick the timer model. For example, a 10 by 12 foot bedroom is 120 square feet, well inside the 230 to 280 square foot ratings here.

The BeOkay holds 58 oz and the TABYIK 35 oz. Plate output is small, so the tank sets how long the unit runs before shutoff. If you leave for work, take the larger tank. Think about the worst day, such as a rainy weekend with the door shut, and size the tank to that.

The BeOkay says 230 sq ft, the TABYIK 280 and the OWAAE 1000. A plate cannot treat 1000 square feet of damp air, so favour the modest claims and use the large ones as ceilings. Ratings from 230 to 1000 square feet assume a mild problem, so a bathroom with a daily shower should count as half the area.

A plate loses output as air cools and can frost. The Newo, BeOkay and Windangel list auto defrost. None belongs in an unheated garage. If the room dips under about 60 degrees at night, expect the plate to slow and the defrost to cycle.

Plate units are quiet by design. The OWAAE claims under 30 dB in sleep mode. For bedrooms, sleep mode matters more than tank size. Remember that fan noise rises when the unit fills, because airflow works harder.

Every unit here moves ounces, not pints. If you see mould or a musty smell that persists, you need a compressor machine, which sits above this cap. A last check is whether the damp has an obvious source, such as a leak or a dryer vent, since fixing it beats any appliance.

specDecoder.meaning: A preset run time before shutoff. It saves power and prevents running dry. It lets you leave without leaving the unit running empty.
Volume before shutoff. It sets unattended run time. It sets how long the unit works before it stops.
A seller estimate for a closed room. Treat it as the biggest room the seller will claim.

howWeEvaluated.title: Control and run time
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared timers, modes and tank size. The Newo led on timers and the BeOkay on tank. Timers were scored by how many options the unit gives, not by the claimed number of hours.

howWeEvaluated.title: Claim realism
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked room ratings against the technology. Modest claims scored higher. Tank size counted only when paired with a working auto shutoff.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cold-room behaviour
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for defrost. Three units list it. We treated any mention of defrost as a positive for cool rooms.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered sleep modes and the OWAAE's under 30 dB claim. Sleep mode and a quiet fan scored best for bedrooms.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on spec sheets and listing feedback patterns, we weighed leaks, fading output and noise. Recurring reports of leaks and early fan failure lowered a score.

howToChoose.note: Measure the room first: anything over about 250 square feet or with an open doorway is beyond what these plates can treat.
The price gaps between these units are small, so choose on the feature you will actually use rather than on the lowest number.

cards.label: Timers
cards.text: The Newo lets you set 24 to 96 hours and shuts off by itself.

cards.label: Big tank
cards.text: The BeOkay holds 58 oz and runs longer before shutoff.

howToChoose.note: Pick timers if you travel; pick the tank if you are home daily. If you are home most days and empty the tank by habit, the larger tank wins; if you travel, the Newo timers do.
Check noise in your own room for the first night, since a sleep-mode figure is measured in a quiet lab and furniture changes how it sounds.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Timers, defrost and a tank you can empty easily.

howToChoose.note: Put the unit near the source of moisture, with the door closed, for the best chance of a visible result.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The room is damp or cool. A compressor is the right tool.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only need a closet fix. The TABYIK is enough.

maintenance.why: Slime forms where water sits. Skipping it leaves a film that smells musty within weeks.
Dust restricts airflow. Dust over the vent raises plate temperature and cuts output.
Removes film from the tank. Plain white vinegar works and leaves no residue.
Small units run long hours. A warm or frayed cord is a reason to retire the unit.
Trapped water breeds mould. Leave the tank open for a day before packing it away.

faq.q: Which is better, the Newo or the BeOkay?
faq.a: The Newo has longer timers, and the BeOkay has a larger tank. If you cannot decide, choose the one whose control scheme you understand without reading the manual.

faq.q: What budget do I need for a basement?
faq.a: A basement needs a compressor machine, which sits above this cap. Compare the test condition printed beside any output figure before trusting it.
A few seasons of steady use. Careful cleaning matters more to lifespan than the brand name does.

faq.q: Is the 1000 sq ft rating real?
faq.a: Only for mild dampness in a closed room. These ratings are fine for a closet and generous for a bedroom.
No, they are decoration and can be turned off. Switch them off at night to avoid light in a sleeping room.
Yes, with auto shutoff and a flat surface. Never run any of them on a bed, sofa or thick rug.
